title: ⚔️ Chapter boss ⭐⭐⭐: words, proofs and titles

questions.prompt: Sami is building his paragraph. He has written: "My grandfather watches the birds every morning, and my cousin sits in the yard reading his newspaper." Three of the four word fields are already there. Which field does he still have to use?

options.text: ANIMALS
FAMILY
FOOD
LEISURE

questions.explanation: The sentence names his grandfather and his cousin (FAMILY), the birds (ANIMALS) and reading (LEISURE), so the field Sami still has to use is FOOD: a word such as vegetables, grapes or a recipe would fill it. A word field is a family of words about one subject, and a full paragraph puts all four of them to work.

questions.prompt: Anis is seventeen, and he laughs and blocks his ears when his sister tells him he is wrong. His little brother is five, and he draws on the kitchen wall when nobody is watching. Which sentence describes the two of them?

options.text: Anis is childish and his brother is naughty.
Anis is naughty and his brother is childish.
Anis is naughty and his brother is sensible.
Anis is sensitive and his brother is naughty.

questions.explanation: "Anis is childish and his brother is naughty." is the right pair: childish is for somebody who behaves like a small child at an age when he should not, and naughty is kept for a badly behaved small child. The classic mistake is "Anis is naughty and his brother is childish.", which swaps the two words: a boy of five cannot behave like a small child, because he is one. "Anis is naughty and his brother is sensible." calls a wall-drawing five-year-old reasonable, and "Anis is sensitive and his brother is naughty." says that Anis's feelings are easily hurt, which no fact here shows.

questions.prompt: Amina checks the bus timetable the evening before a journey, and she always keeps a little money for an emergency. Which sentence describes her?

options.text: Amina is childish.
Amina is sensible.
Amina is sensitive.
Amina is sympathetic.

questions.explanation: "Amina is sensible." is the one: in English sensible means reasonable, and planning ahead and keeping money for an emergency is exactly that. "Amina is sensitive." would say that her feelings are easily hurt, "Amina is sympathetic." that she is sorry for somebody who suffers, and "Amina is childish." that she behaves like a small child. Here only the situation decides, never the shape of the word.

questions.prompt: Rania has written this paragraph for her English notebook: "I keep my grandmother's old radio on the shelf above my bed. I put it on at seven, before school, and again in the evening when I am reading. I like slow songs with a violin in them, and I know every word of them. My cousin Skander plays the oud and wants me to learn, but I would rather listen. On Fridays my mum does the cooking, and the radio stays on the kitchen table until we have finished." Which title from your book's list fits her paragraph?

options.text: Cooking
Learning and playing music
Leisure activities
My favourite music

questions.explanation: "My favourite music" is the title: the radio and the songs Rania listens to hold every sentence together, from seven in the morning to the kitchen table on Friday. "Learning and playing music" belongs to her cousin Skander, who plays the oud, while Rania says she would rather listen. "Cooking" is true of the Friday sentence alone, and a title is never one detail. The classic mistake is "Leisure activities", so wide that it would fit almost any paragraph.

questions.prompt: Nabil's cousin describes him: "My cousin Nabil is fifteen and lives two streets away. Every Saturday he cleans the yard of the old lady on the corner, and she gives him grapes from her garden. He knows everybody between the bakery and the school, and he stops to talk to them all. He watched my uncle repair an old bicycle once, and the next week he repaired mine alone. He still wants the biggest piece of cake, though, and he complains all evening if his sister takes it." Which fact proves that Nabil is sociable?

options.text: He cleans the old lady's yard every Saturday.
He stops to talk to everybody in the street.
He repaired the bicycle after watching it once.
He complains all evening about a piece of cake.

questions.explanation: Sociable means enjoying the company of other people, so the proof is "He stops to talk to everybody in the street." "He cleans the old lady's yard every Saturday." proves that he is kind, "He repaired the bicycle after watching it once." proves that he is bright, and "He complains all evening about a piece of cake." proves that he is childish. The classic mistake is to prove an adjective with a second adjective: "he is sociable because he is nice" proves nothing at all.

questions.prompt: Maher is writing about his Saturdays. Which sentence is correct English?

options.text: I play guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the musics in her room.
I play the guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the musics in her room.
I play guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the music in her room.
I play the guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the music in her room.

questions.explanation: "I play the guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the music in her room." is right on both points: play takes the before the name of an instrument, and music is uncountable, so it never takes an -s. "I play guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the music in her room." drops the article the instrument needs, "I play the guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the musics in her room." puts an -s on an uncountable word, and "I play guitar in the morning, and my sister listens to the musics in her room." makes both mistakes at once.
